name: domain-driven-hexagon — TypeScript modular monolith
description: A NestJS application organised as feature modules over shared domain, application and infrastructure libraries. It already has interface-layer, application-layer and domain-layer dependency rules enforced by dependency-cruiser, which makes it a test of whether an agent recognises existing enforcement instead of selling it back as new work.
softwareCategory: Single-deployable NestJS application with feature modules and shared libraries
architectureFamily: Hexagonal / clean-architecture layering (api, application, domain, database) expressed through NestJS modules and dependency-cruiser rules
expectedCharacteristics: Two feature modules with their own domain, application, database, dto and mapping code
Shared building blocks in src/libs: ddd primitives, application context, api adapters, db adapters, ports, decorators, exceptions and types
Composition through NestJS modules and dependency-injection tokens, not a hand-written composition root
Existing .dependency-cruiser.js rules that enforce layer direction (api/application/domain/infrastructure)
package.json is private, so the library profile's publishable-evidence requirement is not met
profileNotes: package.json declares "private": true. The library profile requires publishable evidence, so it does not apply; a correct assessment says so rather than declaring it.

expectedBoundaries.rationale: A feature module with commands, queries, domain, database, dto and DI tokens of its own.
A second feature module with application, domain and database code.
Entity, aggregate-root and value-object primitives shared by the feature modules.
Declared port interfaces that adapters implement.
Persistence adapters live beside the modules they serve and with the shared db helpers.
Application modules, configuration and bootstrap wiring are the composition area; the framework owns instantiation.

expectedObservations.statement: Dependency-cruiser rules already enforce layer direction, and package.json exposes deps:validate.
There is no ACIMA unit map, so ACIMA's own rules are not measurable until units are declared.
The package is private, so the library profile cannot be claimed for the shared libraries.
Feature modules (user, wallet) are distinct from shared libraries under src/libs.

Composition is framework-managed: NestJS modules and DI tokens instantiate components, so ACIMA's explicit-registration requirement needs a framework-aware reading rather than a hand-written composition root.

knownLimitations: No violation-level ground truth is recorded, so finding precision and recall are reported unavailable rather than estimated.
The repository is not published and the ACIMA enforcer is not configured for it, so there is no second finding set to cross-check.
A correct unit map may reasonably merge or split the shared libraries; boundary scoring accepts the declared alternatives but does not prove one map is optimal.
The TypeScript enforcer analyses source text, not resolved module graphs.

groundTruth.method: Manual inspection of the pinned checkout: package manifest, module layout, dependency-cruiser configuration and NestJS module files.
groundTruth.notes: The existing dependency-cruiser rules were read directly from the pinned commit so the 'already enforced' observation is evidence-backed rather than inferred from the README.
